Installing updates on phones with Google Play

Google plans to expand developer verification globally in 2027 on certified Android devices. Neutrodyne isn’t registered. When verification applies, use the one-time advanced flow in Developer options: Allow apps from unverified developers. It includes a restart and a 24-hour wait. Choose indefinitely; choosing 7 days means repeating it for later updates. The initial regional participating-store rollout does not block direct GitHub installs. Phones without Google certification, such as GrapheneOS or LineageOS, are not affected. No exact global date is known.

If you chose 7 days in Allow apps from unverified developers, future updates stop working after that period. Choose indefinitely in Developer options to keep installing updates. Phones without Google certification do not need this setting.

Choose the file for your device. The arm64-v8a and x86_64 APKs include YouTube playback; armeabi-v7a opens YouTube externally. A 64-bit phone can install the matching 64-bit APK over a 32-bit install and keep its library.

Get releases only from the repository’s GitHub releases page. Windows 10 22H2 or 11: x64 ZIP or MSI if published, also on Windows 11 on Arm through x64 emulation. Apple Silicon macOS 13+: ZIP before 1.0, DMG from 1.0. Linux x64 or arm64: DEB, RPM or tar.gz, glibc 2.31+. Intel Macs, 32-bit desktops and Windows 10 on Arm are unsupported. There are no store or package-catalogue releases.

Compare the file’s SHA-256 with SHA256SUMS or the update card. On Linux use sha256sum FILE; on macOS shasum -a 256 FILE; on Windows PowerShell Get-FileHash FILE -Algorithm SHA256. A matching checksum detects damage, not a fake release. For GitHub attestations use gh attestation verify FILE --repo REPO (replace REPO with the repository below). Exact OpenJDK and LGPL component sources accompany releases.

Published Android APKs are optimized, non-debuggable release builds signed with the public key committed in this repository. Anyone can use that key: download only from our GitHub releases. Local debug builds use ch.lkmc.neutrodyne.debug and are never published. Moving to a private key would require reinstalling; back up first.
Install and update from your browser

Open the APK downloaded by your browser. Android asks you to allow that browser or file manager to install unknown apps (a per-source permission). Allow it, return to the APK and confirm. Install updates over the existing app to keep subscriptions, groups, positions, queue, settings and downloads. Neutrodyne only checks GitHub and notifies you; it never downloads or installs updates.
Systems without Google certification, such as GrapheneOS or LineageOS, are not subject to Google developer verification. Install the APK as usual. Neutrodyne cannot reliably detect certification.

For experienced users: from a computer use adb install -r FILE.apk to keep your data. ADB installs are exempt from developer verification. Turn USB debugging off afterwards. Installers using Shizuku may also work; restart Shizuku after each reboot, and remember that future Android changes may affect it.

Add this repository to Obtainium. Choose its architecture filter or an APK filter such as neutrodyne-.*-arm64-v8a\.apk$. Turn off Neutrodyne’s automatic check in Settings > Updates if desired. Check now still works. Obtainium is subject to developer verification like other installers.

Android Auto: every Neutrodyne install comes from GitHub. In Android Auto settings, open About and tap Version and permission info 10 times to enable developer mode. Open developer settings and enable Unknown sources. Neutrodyne then appears in Auto. The Desktop Head Unit needs the same setting. Availability on retail Android Automotive OS cars is unverified.

On Apple Silicon with macOS 13+, unzip the 0.x ZIP and move Neutrodyne.app to Applications. From 1.0, open the DMG and drag the app to Applications. On first launch, cancel the warning, open System Settings > Privacy & Security, choose Open Anyway and authenticate. The app is unsigned and not notarized. Repeat Open Anyway after each update. Quit Neutrodyne, replace the app in Applications and reopen it. Your library stays in its data folder.

On Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11, run the x64 MSI if published, or extract the portable ZIP. Windows 11 on Arm uses the x64 build through emulation. SmartScreen: More info > Run anyway; it may ask again for every update. If Smart App Control blocks the unsigned app, it cannot allow just this app. Use another supported system or turn Smart App Control off only after considering the system-wide effect; turning it back on can require reinstalling Windows. Quit Neutrodyne before running a newer MSI or extracting over the old ZIP folder. Your data stays outside that folder.

Choose x64 or arm64 for your machine (glibc 2.31+). Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install ./FILE.deb. Fedora: sudo dnf install ./FILE.rpm. For tar.gz, quit Neutrodyne and extract in place of the old folder. Install the next release the same way. Data remains in your user data directory.

On Windows Neutrodyne enables Java Access Bridge for NVDA. If NVDA cannot read it, create %USERPROFILE%/.accessibility.properties containing assistive_technologies=com.sun.java.accessibility.AccessBridge and restart Neutrodyne. macOS uses VoiceOver. Screen readers are not supported on Linux: the user-interface toolkit Neutrodyne uses has no Linux accessibility support yet. Keyboard navigation, scaling and the high-contrast themes work.

Remove the app or portable folder. Your data is kept separately: Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%/Neutrodyne; macOS ~/Library/Application Support/ch.lkmc.neutrodyne; Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/neutrodyne (normally ~/.local/share/neutrodyne). Back up before manually deleting these folders.

Neutrodyne’s maintainers chose not to register with Google or obtain Apple Developer ID or Microsoft signing. These choices require manual installation steps. Read the repository README for the reasons.
Download only from this repository’s GitHub releases page. Choose arm64-v8a or x86_64 for a 64-bit phone, armeabi-v7a for a 32-bit phone. There is no store version.

Desktop packages are unsigned and not notarized. Windows and macOS warn for each new version. They bundle an unmodified OpenJDK runtime and LGPL FFmpeg; exact sources accompany the release. MSI may be unavailable; use ZIP if no MSI is published.
The version line shows your system, architecture, package format and runtime. Windows 11 on Arm uses x64 emulation.

If Android refuses an unverified install, your installed version keeps working.

1. Open Settings > About phone and tap Build number 7 times.
2. Open System > Developer options > Allow apps from unverified developers.
3. Continue only if installing was your own decision. The confirmation helps prevent coercion by scammers.
4. Restart the phone and wait 24 hours.
5. Confirm with your fingerprint or PIN. Choose indefinitely; choosing 7 days stops later updates after a week.
6. Reopen the APK and confirm the warning. Menu names vary by manufacturer. Devices without Google certification need none of this. ADB remains an alternative.
